t: Section 509(c) of the Housing Act of 1949 is amended by striking out “within eighteen months after such date of enactment ’ in the first sentence and inserting in lieu thereof “within thirty-six months after such date of enactment”.

fable.w: This section only extends a statutory deadline from eighteen to thirty-six months by amending existing text. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Whatever section 509(c) itself requires is not stated in this text, so nothing here recommends or requires participation.

opus.w: This amendment only extends a time period in Section 509(c), from eighteen to thirty-six months. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Even if the deadline is for outside parties asking for assistance, that is an application for a benefit, which the definition excludes.
opus.s: striking out “within eighteen months after such date of enactment ’ in the first sentence and inserting in lieu thereof “within thirty-six months after such date of enactment”
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Section 509 of the Housing Act of 1949 deals with federal help for homeowners, and the deadline being changed may be the time an outside party has to ask the Secretary for that help. So it might look like it gives outsiders a role in a federal decision.

2. **Why it fails:** The section only changes a time limit from eighteen to thirty-six months. It doesn't create a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Even if the deadline is for homeowners asking for help, that is a request for a benefit, which the definition excludes.
